section_summary.extract_value: This section details the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) used in the current study, specifying it was the original 13-item version. It highlights the scale's psychometric properties, including its invariance for U.S. men and women and satisfactory validity in previous studies of U.S. college students, and reports internal consistency reliability for women and men in the current sample.
section_summary.evidence_source: The Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos et al., 2005) was used to assess positive body image. The original 13-item measure was used because the second version ofthe measure (the Body Appreciation Scale-2; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b) was not available at the time of data collection. Although the BAS was initially created for use with women, scores on the scale were found to be invariant for U.S. men and women (Tylka, 2013), with differential item responding on one item. BAS scores have demonstrated satisfactory validity and reliability in previous studies of U.S. college students (Avalos et al., 2005; Tylka, 2013). Internal consistency reliability scores in the current study were adequate (Cronbach's ˛: women ˛= .92, men ˛= .90).
